summary: Richard B. Mahoney works in Buddhist studies and computational fields. He completed an MA at the University of Canterbury by 2002 under supervisor Paul Harrison and held a post there in 2001.
Richard B. Martin is a scholar of Tibetology and Indology. He served at the University of Virginia as a professor (attested 1983–1991) and later as South Asian bibliographer (attested 2003).

Richard Baker is a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied at Harvard, UC Berkeley, and under Shunryu Suzuki in 1961. He founded the San Francisco Zen Center in 1962, served as its abbot (1971–1984), and founded Dharma Sangha.

Richard Barron works in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, and Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge.

Richard Bowring is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned his BA, doctorate, and Litt.D at Cambridge. He taught at Columbia, Princeton, and Cambridge, and served as Master of Selwyn College (2000–2012).

Richard Carnac Temple (1850–1931) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Trinity Hall, Cambridge, served in the Bengal and Indian Staff Corps, edited the Indian Antiquary (~1885–1931), and founded Panjab Notes and Queries (1883).
Richard D. Mann works in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at McMaster University under Phyllis Granoff (attested 2003) and held a post at Carleton University (attested 2007).

Richard D. McBride II specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a PhD from UCLA in 2001, mentored by Robert E. Buswell Jr., and held posts at Dongguk University and Brigham Young University.

Richard Delbrueck (1875–1957) was an archaeologist who studied at the University of Bonn (~1895–1899). He held professorial and academic posts at the University of Jena (~1911–1915), University of Giessen (~1922–1928), and University of Bonn (~1928–1940).

Richard F. Nance works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. After completing his PhD at the University of Chicago in 2004, he held assistant and associate professor posts in religious studies at Indiana University Bloomington.

Richard Fick (1867–1944) was an Indologist who studied at Kiel University. He worked at Kiel University Library, the Royal Library of Berlin, and was director of the Göttingen State and University Library while at the University of Göttingen (1921–1932).

Richard Foltz is a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies, religion, and history. Educated at the University of Utah and Harvard (PhD 1996), he taught at Kuwait, Brown, Columbia, and Florida before joining Concordia University (~2006–2026).
Richard Fritzsche (born 1851) was an Indologist. He studied under Hermann Brockhaus from ~1873 to 1877 and served as rector at Gymnasium Schneeberg from ~1888 to 1916.

Richard G. Salomon works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. A former student of Ludo Rocher (~1970–1975), he served as a professor and Professor Emeritus of Sanskrit at the University of Washington from ~1981 to ~2019.

Richard Gombrich is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oxford (BA, DPhil) and under K. R. Norman. He served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1965–2004) and President of the Pali Text Society (1994–2002).

Richard Hartshorne (1899–1992) studied at Princeton (~1916–1920) and the University of Chicago (~1921–1924). He held academic posts at the University of Minnesota (~1924–1940) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1940–1970).

Richard Hauschild (1901–1972) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübingen, Leipzig (under Johannes Hertel), and Jena (under Albert Debrunner). He served as Lektor and later Professor at the University of Jena (1951–1967).

Richard Henebry (1863–1916) was a linguist who studied at St. John's College, Waterford, St Patrick's Pontifical University, Maynooth, the University of Greifswald, and the University of Freiburg, studying under Heinrich Zimmer (~1896–1898).

Richard Hugh Robinson (1926–1970) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Alberta and the University of London under Arthur Waley and David Friedman, later teaching at Toronto and becoming Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1961).

Richard Hughes Seager works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin System, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD), and was Associate Professor of Religion at Hamilton College around 1994.
